verses.text: Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may spread quickly and be held in honor, just as it was with you.

xrefs.text: Brothers, pray for us as well.
as you pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.
because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me.
Pray also for me, that whenever I open my mouth, words may be given me so that I will boldly make known the mystery of the gospel,
So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.
But the word of God continued to spread and multiply.
For not only did the message of the Lord ring out from you to Macedonia and Achaia, but your faith in God has gone out to every place, so that we have no need to say anything more.
Pray without ceasing.

notes.note: General Information: In verses 1–5, Paul asks the believers to pray for him and his companions and encourages them. A heading for this section might be, “Pray for Us.”

Here, the word Finally marks a change in topic. To pray is not the final instruction that Paul gives but it is how Paul opens the last section of his letter where he will discuss a few remaining matters. Alternate translation: [One more thing] or [So, continuing on]
Here, brothers means fellow Christians, including both men and women. Alternate translation: [brothers and sisters]
The pronoun us refers to Paul and his companions. If you have exclusive and inclusive first person pronouns in your language, this should be an exclusive pronoun.

Paul speaks of God’s word spreading as if it were running from place to place. He is comparing the rapid spread of God’s word to a person who takes good news to others. Alternate translation: [might spread rapidly] or [might be heard by many people]
You can state this in active form, if the passive construction is not natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and that many people would honor it]

This phrase leaves out some words that many languages might need to be complete. If it would be helpful in your language, you could supply these words from the context. Alternate translation: [just as also happened with you] or [which is exactly what you did]

verses.text: And pray that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men; for not everyone holds to the faith.

xrefs.text: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.
Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there,
He said: “I will hide My face from them; I will see what will be their end. For they are a perverse generation— children of unfaithfulness.
But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
I tell you, He will promptly carry out justice on their behalf. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin. But you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.
But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and they blasphemously contradicted what Paul was saying.
We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.

notes.note: You can state this in active form. Alternate translation: [God may save us] or [God may rescue us]

The two terms perverse and evil mean basically the same thing and are used together to emphasize the amount of evil. If your language does not use repetition to do this or if you do not have two words for these attributes, you can use one phrase and provide emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [very wicked men] or [many wicked men]

The phrase not everyone is a negative understatement that emphasizes how rare faith is. If this is confusing in your language, you can express the meaning positively. Alternate translation: [for only some people believe in the Lord] or [for people who believe in Jesus are few]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of faith, you can express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [believes in Jesus]

verses.text: But the Lord is faithful, and He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.

xrefs.text: And the Lord will rescue me from every evil action and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.

No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.
The LORD will guard you from all evil; He will preserve your soul.
God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful.
I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.
Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling and to present you unblemished in His glorious presence, with great joy—

notes.note: The word strengthen here refers to spiritual strength, not physical strength. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [who will strengthen you spiritually] or [who will make you inwardly strong]
This could mean: (1) the evil being Satan. Alternate translation: [Satan] or (2) evil in general. Alternate translation: [evil]

verses.text: And we have confidence in the Lord that you are doing and will continue to do what we command.

xrefs.text: being confident of this, that He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.
Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.
And you are indeed showing this love to all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to excel more and more
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
I wrote as I did so that on my arrival I would not be grieved by those who ought to make me rejoice. I had confidence in all of you, that you would share my joy.
Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from any brother who leads an undisciplined life that is not in keeping with the tradition you received from us.

Finally, brothers, we ask and encourage you in the Lord Jesus to live in a way that is pleasing to God, just as you have received from us. This is how you already live, so you should do so all the more.
We command and urge such people by our Lord Jesus Christ to begin working quietly to earn their own living.

notes.note: The phrase We are also confident may be confusing in some languages. If that is the case in your language, you could translate this as a noun phrase. Alternate translation: [We also have faith] or [We also trust]

notes.quote: πεποίθαμεν δὲ ἐν Κυρίῳ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς
notes.note: This could mean: (1) Paul has confidence in the Thessalonian believers because of the close relationship that they have with the Lord Jesus. In this case, Paul is speaking of this relationship as if they were inside the Lord Jesus. Alternate translation: [Because you are united to the Lord, we are also confident]; (2) Paul has confidence in the Lord Jesus, that he will cause them to do what is right. Alternate translation: [Because we trust in the Lord Jesus to enable you, we are also confident]

named.name: LORD
named.brief: Names or title used to refer to God

verses.text: May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love and Christ’s perseverance.

xrefs.text: Turn my heart to Your testimonies and not to covetous gain.
O LORD, God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, keep this desire forever in the intentions of the hearts of Your people, and direct their hearts toward You.
The LORD your God will circumcise your hearts and the hearts of your descendants, and you will love Him with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.
We love because He first loved us.
Because you have kept My command to persevere, I will also keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth.
Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy set before Him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
But the one who loves God is known by God.

“But this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD. I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.

notes.quote: ὁ & Κύριος κατευθύναι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας εἰς τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ εἰς τὴν ὑπομονὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ
notes.note: Here, hearts stands for a person’s thoughts or mind. If your readers would not understand this, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [may the Lord cause you to understand the love of God and the endurance of Christ] or [may the Lord help you to know the love of God and the endurance of Christ]

notes.quote: εἰς τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ εἰς τὴν ὑπομονὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ
notes.note: Paul speaks of God’s love and Christ’s endurance as if they were destinations on a path. If your readers would not understand this figure of speech, you could express the meaning in a nonfigurative way. Alternate translation: [to know how much God loves you and the endurance that Christ supplies you]

notes.quote: εἰς τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ εἰς τὴν ὑπομονὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ
notes.note: Here, love of God can mean (1) the love that comes from God. Alternate translation: [to know how much God loves you] or (2) the love that people give to God. Alternate translation: [to love God more]

Here, endurance of Christ can mean (1) the endurance that Christ gives to his people. Alternate translation: [to experience the endurance that Christ gives you] or (2) the endurance that Christ had through his suffering. Alternate translation: [to know how much Christ has endured for you]

verses.text: Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from any brother who leads an undisciplined life that is not in keeping with the tradition you received from us.

xrefs.text: For even while we were with you, we gave you this command: “If anyone is unwilling to work, he shall not eat.
For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not undisciplined among you,
And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.
And we urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
Therefore, brothers, stand firm and cling to the traditions we taught you, whether by speech or by letter.
having a form of godliness but denying its power. Turn away from such as these!

Finally, brothers, we ask and encourage you in the Lord Jesus to live in a way that is pleasing to God, just as you have received from us. This is how you already live, so you should do so all the more.

notes.note: General Information: In verses 6–15, Paul gives the believers some final instructions about working and not being idle. A heading for this section might be, “Believers Must Work.”
The word translated Now marks a change in topic. You can use a natural way in your language to show that this is a new section with a different topic than the previous section.
Here, the words brothers and brother refer to fellow Christians, including both men and women. Alternate translation: [brothers and sisters … brother or sister]

notes.quote: ἐν ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
notes.note: Here, name stands for the person of Jesus Christ. It can also mean “with the authority of.” If using this term is not clear in your language, you could express it directly. Alternate translation: [as if our Lord Jesus Christ himself were speaking] or [with the authority that our Lord Jesus Christ has given us]
Here, our refers to all believers. If you have exclusive and inclusive first-person plural pronouns in your language, this should be an inclusive pronoun.

Here Paul speaks of people who are not living well as if they walk in a haphazard manner. If your readers would not understand this metaphor, you could use an equivalent metaphor from your culture. Alternatively, you could express the meaning in a nonfigurative way. Alternate translation: [who is living in a bad way] or [who is not living correctly]
Here, the traditions refers to the teachings that the apostles received from Jesus and are passing along to all believers. Alternate translation: [the teachings] or [the instructions]

verses.text: For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not undisciplined among you,

xrefs.text: Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from any brother who leads an undisciplined life that is not in keeping with the tradition you received from us.
Not that we lack this right, but we wanted to offer ourselves as an example for you to imitate.
Therefore I urge you to imitate me.
You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.
In everything, show yourself to be an example by doing good works. In your teaching show integrity, dignity,
Join one another in following my example, brothers, and carefully observe those who walk according to the pattern we set for you.
And you became imitators of us and of the Lord when you welcomed the message with the joy of the Holy Spirit, in spite of your great suffering.
Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.

notes.note: The phrase to imitate may be a difficult word to translate in your language. In that case, you could make this explicit. Alternate translation: [to act the way that my fellow workers and I act]

Paul uses a double negative to emphasize the positive. If this double negative would be misunderstood in your language, you could translate it as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [we lived among you as those who had much discipline] or [we worked diligently when we were with you]

verses.text: nor did we eat anyone’s food without paying for it. Instead, in labor and toil, we worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to any of you.

xrefs.text: Give us this day our daily bread.
Surely you recall, brothers, our labor and toil. We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to anyone while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.
He who has been stealing must steal no longer, but must work, doing good with his own hands, that he may have something to share with the one in need.
and to aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands, as we instructed you.
We work hard with our own hands. When we are vilified, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it;
She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
We command and urge such people by our Lord Jesus Christ to begin working quietly to earn their own living.

notes.note: Paul refers to bread here because it was the most common and basic food for them. If your readers would not be familiar with bread or if that is a kind of food that would be considered unusual or extravagant, you could use a general expression for ordinary food. Alternate translation: [food] or [anything]

Here, night and day forms a merism, which means “all the time.” If it would be helpful in your language to explain that they did not work without taking any rest whatsoever, then you could make the meaning clear. Alternate translation: [working throughout that time with little rest] or [we worked almost continuously]

Here, toil and hardship have very similar meanings. Paul used this repetition to emphasize that they worked very hard. If you do not have two similar words that you can use here or if it would be unnatural for you to use such repetition, you could emphasize this in another way. Alternate translation: [with great effort] or [in very difficult circumstances]

verses.text: Not that we lack this right, but we wanted to offer ourselves as an example for you to imitate.

xrefs.text: For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not undisciplined among you,
Have we no right to food and to drink?
Nor did we seek praise from you or from anyone else, although as apostles of Christ we had authority to demand it.
Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word must share in all good things with his instructor.
I have set you an example so that you should do as I have done for you.
Take no bag for the road, or second tunic, or sandals, or staff; for the worker is worthy of his provisions.
For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in His footsteps:

notes.quote: οὐχ ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν, ἀλλ’
notes.note: Paul uses a double negative to emphasize the positive. If this double negative would be misunderstood in your language, you could translate it as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [and we certainly have the right to receive food from you, but instead we worked for our food]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of example, you can express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [we might show you the right way in order for you] or [we might demonstrate the way to live for you]
See how you translated imitate in verse 7.

verses.text: For even while we were with you, we gave you this command: “If anyone is unwilling to work, he shall not eat.

xrefs.text: By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground— because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
The slacker craves yet has nothing, but the soul of the diligent is fully satisfied.
and to aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands, as we instructed you.
The slacker does not plow in season; at harvest time he looks, but nothing is there.
The craving of the slacker kills him because his hands refuse to work.
I went past the field of a slacker and by the vineyard of a man lacking judgment.
Indeed, when we were with you, we kept warning you that we would suffer persecution; and as you know, it has come to pass.

notes.quote: εἴ τις οὐ θέλει ἐργάζεσθαι, μηδὲ ἐσθιέτω
notes.note: You can state this in positive form, if this form is difficult to understand in your language. Alternate translation: [If a person wants to eat, he must work]

verses.text: For we hear that some of you are leading undisciplined lives, accomplishing nothing, but being busybodies.

xrefs.text: At the same time they will also learn to be idle, going from house to house and being not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, discussing things they should not mention.
Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from any brother who leads an undisciplined life that is not in keeping with the tradition you received from us.
and to aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands, as we instructed you.
Indeed, none of you should suffer as a murderer or thief or wrongdoer, or even as a meddler.

notes.note: Here, walking stands for behavior in life. you can use an equivalent metaphor from your culture, if it is available. Otherwise, you could express the meaning in a nonfigurative way. Alternate translation: [some who are living idle lives] or [some who are being lazy]
Meddlers are people who interfere in the affairs of others without being asked to help.

verses.text: We command and urge such people by our Lord Jesus Christ to begin working quietly to earn their own living.

xrefs.text: He who has been stealing must steal no longer, but must work, doing good with his own hands, that he may have something to share with the one in need.
and to aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands, as we instructed you.
nor did we eat anyone’s food without paying for it. Instead, in labor and toil, we worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to any of you.
Better a dry morsel in quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.
Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.
Give us each day our daily bread.
Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.

Finally, brothers, we ask and encourage you in the Lord Jesus to live in a way that is pleasing to God, just as you have received from us. This is how you already live, so you should do so all the more.

notes.note: Here, with quietness is the opposite of meddling. Paul exhorts the meddlers to stop getting involved in other people’s affairs. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of quietness, you can express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in a quiet and peaceful manner]

verses.text: But as for you, brothers, do not grow weary in well-doing.

xrefs.text: Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
Consider Him who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.
Therefore, since God in His mercy has given us this ministry, we do not lose heart.
He gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak.
Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart:
And you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord, and do not lose heart when He rebukes you.
Without growing weary, you have persevered and endured many things for the sake of My name.

notes.note: Paul here uses the word But to contrast the lazy believers with the hardworking believers. Use a natural way in your language for introducing a contrast. Alternate translation: [Concerning]
The word you refers to all the Thessalonian believers, so it should be in plural form.
Here, brothers means fellow Christians, including both men and women. Alternate translation: [brothers and sisters]

verses.text: Take note of anyone who does not obey the instructions we have given in this letter. Do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.

But now I am writing you not to associate with anyone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler. With such a man do not even eat.
Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, O LORD.
Anyone, then, who rejects this command does not reject man but God, the very One who gives you His Holy Spirit.

Are they ashamed of the abomination they have committed? No, they have no shame at all; they do not even know how to blush. So they will fall among the fallen; when I punish them, they will collapse,” says the LORD.
I did not listen to the voice of my teachers or incline my ear to my mentors.
She heeded no voice; she accepted no correction. She does not trust in the LORD; she has not drawn near to her God.

notes.note: Paul is referring to his command to the Thessalonian believers as a word. If your readers would not understand this, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [our instructions]
Paul wants the Thessalonians to notice who this person is. Alternate translation: [point out that person] or [make sure everyone knows who he is]

Paul instructs believers to avoid lazy believers as a disciplinary action. If necessary, you could make this explicit to make the meaning clear. Alternate translation: [in order that he will know that his laziness is wrong]

hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the Day of the Lord.

“Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and they will call Him Immanuel” (which means, “God with us”
Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled; do not be afraid.

The word translated Now marks a change in topic. You can use a natural way in your language to show that this is a new section with a different topic than the previous section.

notes.quote: αὐτὸς & ὁ Κύριος τῆς εἰρήνης, δῴη ὑμῖν
notes.note: Paul ends the letter with blessings that are also prayers. Use a form that people would recognize as a blessing or prayer in your language. Alternate translation: [I pray that the Lord of peace himself may give you]
